In case the date of constitution / incorporation of the OEM is less than 3 year old, the average turnover in respect of the completed financial years after the date of constitution shall be taken into account for this criteria. In respect of bid for Services, the bidder must be the Service provider of the offered Service. Relevant documentary evidence in this regard shall be uploaded along with the bid in respect of the offered product or service, and Buyer will decide eligibility based on documentary evidence submitted, while evaluating the bid. Benefits of MSE will be allowed only if seller is validated on-line in GeM profile as well as validated and approved by Buyer after evaluation of documents submitted. 17. Prohibits either party from sharing sensitive contract details, designs or specifications w ith third parties without consent. 8. Price Variation Clause (PVC). Included in long-term contract (over 38 months) to adjust pieces based on changes in the cost of labour or raw materials using government indices. 9. Exchange Rate Variation (ERV). Protects Indian Vendors from currency fluctuations for imported com po nents in contracts lasting over a year. 10. Denial Clause. If a Seller is delayed, the buyer will not pay for any price or tax increases that occur d u ring the extension period, but will take the benefit of any price decreases. 11. Repeat Order. Allows a fresh order for upto 50% of the original quantity within six months of contract c ompletion, provided prices haven't dropped. 12. Risk and Expense purchase. If a seller fails to deliver, the buyer can purchase form another source and recover the extra cost from the original, defaulting seller. 13. Fall Clause. Ensures the Seller does not sell the same item to any other entity at a lower price than w h at is charged in the current contract. 14. Apportionment of Quantity. Used to split a large order between multiple vendors (like L1 & L2) if th e lo west bidder doesn't have the capacity to supply everything. 15. Tolerance Clause. To take care of any change in the requirement during the period starting from issu e of RFP till placement of the contract in exceptional circumstances due to reasons to be recorded which w e re not considered during the planning stage as well seeking AON for the CFA, a plus/minus tolerance claus e (upto 25%) may be incorporated in the RFP, reserving the buyer's right to increase or decrease the quan tity of the required goods/ services up to that limit without any changes in the terms, conditions and per-u nit prices quoted by the seller. While awarding the contract, the quantity ordered can be increased or decr eased by the Buyer within this tolerance limit. However, due care is to be exercised while specifying the to lerance limits in individual cases, since higher the limit, more is the uncertainty for the bidders in formulati ng their prices, which may result in the bidders quoting higher prices. 16.
